name: Bluewater Gorge
description:
Sat, 30th July 2022
Bluewater Gorge
Image credit @wanderstories.
Leader: Luen Warneke
Rated: Hard – rough terrain.
Meeting: Meeting location and time to be emailed.
Distance - 8-10 kilometres return
Time - approximately 4-5 hours return

Walk Description:
The club has done this walk several times in the long distant past.
The terrain is tough and the bush bashing hard - expect now the trail has now been recut. 
There is a bit of lantana, vines, native ginger, long guinea grass, fallen trees/branches on the rough route. It traverse creeks and small gullies. 

The Townsville Bushwalking Club walked from Keelbottom Creek to Bluewater Gorge in 2010. We have also done the Twin Gorges Walk which links up Bluewater Gorge and Patterson Gorge.

How long:
Now it takes half a day since the trail has recently been cut.. Estimate back at the car park around 11am for a 3-5 hour day.

What to bring:
Day pack, food/snacks for the day, water 3 lt minimum (you can refill from creeks - please carry water treatment tablets), long sleeve clothing and good rugged footwear (to protect from sun, scratches, stings, and bites), electrolytes, insect repellent (leeches, mozzies), hat, sunscreen, personal first aid kit (basic), and sunglasses. Also, head torch and whistle.

Must be over 18yrs to participate.

name: Ladies Route, Castle Hill
description:
Leader: Luen Warneke
Image credit @wanderstories
Rated: Medium. Steep bush tracks, uneven footings, with off-track walking. About 2 hours bushwalking.
Meeting time: 7am
Meeting place: email info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com

Have you heard of the Ladies' Route? According to rumour, it's aptly named The Ladies' Route by one of our club members because it was the track that 'female friends' took to visit the soldiers manning the Pillar Boxes on the top of Castle Hill during WWII.

This un-signposted trail is now overgrown, especially in the wet season, however the footpad can be made out in places as it was well-formed with stone stairs and retaining walls.

Returning back to the trail head before lunch. 

What to bring:
half day pack, food/snacks, water 2 to 3 lt, sun protective clothing and good appropriate footwear, hat, sunscreen, personal first aid kit (basic), and sunglasses. 

Fees: non-members $5

Must be over 18yrs to participate.

To RSVP, fill out this form https://forms.gle/bsYRRXLtGBbyZDZ88 
and email the club at info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com

name: Paluma Dam to Jourama Falls
description:
Sun, 17th July 2022
Paluma Dam to Jourama Falls
Image credit: @wanderstories
This is full day bushwalk to Waterfall Creek's top section and it is spectacular! The old-timers called this creek ‘one hundred waterfalls in a day’. 
Leader: Graeme Taylor

Rated: Medium. Long day  

Meeting: Start time 7:30 am. Car shuttles will be required at both Jourama and Paluma dam ends. Meeting point details to be sent out via email to those that RSVP   

Walk Description:
After the car shuttle, the walk will commence at Paluma Dam. Walking through the lush World-Heritage Wet Tropics rainforest along an old logging road and down on a rough single track to Jourama Falls.
Will the group turn off and visit The Black Hole? We’ll make our decision based on how we are tracking for time.
Admire the views from the top of Jourama Falls (and possibly a swim for those who dare) before heading steeply down to Jourama Falls carpark.
The walk finishes at Jourama Falls car park.

How long:
Full day walk. Estimate back at the dam car park around 5 pm, for the car shuttle and drive back to Townsville. Aim for an approximately 8-10 hr day.  

What to bring:
Day pack, food/snacks for the day, water 3 lt minimum (you can refill from creeks - please carry water treatment tablets), long sleeve clothing and good rugged footwear (to protect from sun, scratches, stings, and bites), electrolytes, insect repellent (leeches, mozzies), hat, sunscreen, personal first aid kit (basic), and sunglasses. Also, head torch and whistle. 

Must be over 18yrs to participate.

name: Mt Halifax Summit
description:
Sat, 16th July 2022
Mt Halifax Summit 
Image credit @wanderstories. 

Leader: Jo Wolfinden 

Rated: Hard – rough terrain, steep climbs.  

Meeting: Meeting location and time to be emailed. It will likely be a very early start to make sure we are back before nightfall ideally. 

Walk Description:

This is the highest mountain between Mt Spec at Paluma and Townsville. We often see it shrouded in cloud on our way to Paluma.
The track takes us first along a rocky jungle creek, onto steep boulder-strewn banks and upwards.
The tracks climbs steeply  to the summit of Mt Halifax. There are beautiful waterholes along the way.

How long:
Full day walk. Estimate back at the car park around 5 pm and drive back to Townsville. Aim for a 9-11 hour day. 

What to bring:
Day pack, food/snacks for the day, water 3 lt minimum (you can refill from creeks - please carry water treatment tablets), long sleeve clothing and good rugged footwear (to protect from sun, scratches, stings, and bites), electrolytes, insect repellent (leeches, mozzies), hat, sunscreen, personal first aid kit (basic), and sunglasses. Also, head torch and whistle. 

Must be over 18yrs to participate.

name: Waterfall Creek
description:
Sat, 9th July 2022
Waterfall Creek
This is full day bushwalk to Waterfall Creek's top section and it is spectacular! The old-timers called this creek ‘one hundred waterfalls in a day’. 

Leader: Wilfred Karnoll. 

Rated: Hard – creek-based off-track, rough terrain, steep climbs. 

Walk Description:
The first two hours are track walking, then the next 4 to 5 hours is a creek-based rock hop, followed by the last two hours back on track. The terrain includes uneven footings, rock hopping, scrambling, bush bashing, steep climbs, and some exposed ledges. The return journey is the same route but uphill all the way, with steep climbing in parts (especially straight after lunch). In some areas, there will be tangled vines and wait-a-while. Great views from the waterfall lookout. There will be good swimming opportunities. 

How long:
Full day walk. Estimate back around 5 pm, for the car shuttle and drive back to Townsville.   

What to bring:
Day pack, food/snacks for the day, water 2 lt minimum (refill from creeks- please carry water treatment tablets otherwise carry more water), long sleeve clothing and good rugged footwear (to protect from sun, scratches, stings, and bites), electrolytes, insect repellent (leeches, mozzies), hat, sunscreen, personal first aid kit (basic), and sunglasses. Also, head torch and whistle. 

Must be over 18yrs to participate.
